scenes.headline: How Olmo-core 3 trains a giant MoE
scenes.sub: Open infrastructure for mixture of experts, up to one point two trillion parameters.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Leopold! Olmo-core three is open infrastructure for training big mixture of experts models. It's the system behind the next Olmo, built to scale into the trillions.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Keep every expert resident on its GPU and route each token to the one that holds its expert, instead of re-gathering all the weights.
scenes.say: The idea is simple. Keep every expert resident on its GPU, and send each token to the expert that was chosen for it, instead of gathering all the weights every single step.

steps.say: Each token picks its top experts from the router.
The experts are split across the GPUs. Each token's rows are sent straight to the GPU that holds its expert. That's the all to all dispatch.
The experts run, and the results are gathered back. The weights themselves never move.

scenes.title: Why the old way got slow

left.title: Olmo-core 2
items: Re-gather every expert's weights each step
left.say: Olmo-core two gathered all the expert weights onto every GPU, every small batch. As you add experts, that gets slower and slower.

right.title: Olmo-core 3
right.say: Olmo-core three keeps the experts put and moves only the tokens. Now adding experts stops costing you throughput.

scenes.title: The capacity tax, measured
scenes.note: same active compute per token, very different efficiency
scenes.say: Watch the cost. Under the old sharding, growing the expert pool drops efficiency from forty point nine percent to fifteen point seven, for no extra useful work. With expert parallelism it stays flat.

scenes.label: TFLOP/s/GPU at 1.2T parameters
scenes.note: 38.1% of the B300 peak, on 512 GPUs
scenes.say: At the top end it hits eight hundred fifty eight teraflops per GPU, training a one point two trillion parameter model on five hundred twelve GPUs. About thirty eight percent of the chip's peak.

scenes.text: The hard part of a giant MoE is plumbing: keep experts resident, route the tokens, match the parallelism to the model.
scenes.say: The hard part of training a giant mixture of experts is the plumbing. Keep the experts resident, route the tokens to them, and match the parallelism to the model.

recap: Open code and an honest report
scenes.say: To recap: experts stay resident, tokens get routed, the parallelism is matched to the model, and it's all open.
